name: Balsamic Glazed Chicken with Caprese Protein Pasta
desc: Balsamic-Dijon marinated chicken cutlets over a caprese protein pasta with bacon, finished with a sticky balsamic soy glaze.

source.evidence: Searched for this exact combination (balsamic Dijon marinated cutlets, balsamic soy brown sugar glaze, protein pasta with bacon and mozzarella pearls); only generic caprese chicken pastas with different ingredients turned up.

ingredients.raw: 1 tbsp neutral oil (such as canola or avocado), for the pan
2 tbsp gluten-free soy sauce or tamari
16 oz short-shape protein pasta (such as penne or rotini)
1/2 cup chopped fresh basil, plus more for serving
Freshly cracked black pepper, for serving

steps: Marinate the chicken: Slice the chicken breasts horizontally into cutlets about 3/4 inch thick. In a zip-top bag or bowl, whisk the first 1/3 cup balsamic, the Dijon, lemon juice, garlic, dried basil, oregano, 1 tsp kosher salt, pepper, and 1 tbsp olive oil. Add the chicken, press out the air, and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes and up to 8 hours.
Cook the bacon: Lay the bacon in a cold skillet and set it over medium heat. Cook, flipping once, until crisp, 8-10 minutes. Drain on a paper towel, chop, and pour off all but a thin film of fat.

Boil the pasta: Bring a large pot of well-salted water to a boil and cook the pasta to 1 minute under the package time for al dente, since protein pasta softens as it sits. Reserve 1/2 cup pasta water, drain, and rinse briefly under cold water to stop the cooking.
Mix the glaze: Whisk the cornstarch into the 1/2 cup water until smooth. In a small saucepan, combine the second 1/3 cup balsamic, the soy sauce, brown sugar, and honey.

Simmer the glaze: Bring the saucepan to a gentle simmer over medium heat, then whisk in the cornstarch slurry. Cook, whisking, until it thickens enough to coat a spoon, 1-2 minutes. Take it off the heat; it tightens as it cools, so loosen with a splash of water if it goes past pourable.

Sear the chicken: Heat the neutral oil in a large skillet (use the bacon pan if you like) over medium heat until it shimmers. Shake the excess marinade off the cutlets and lay them in the pan without crowding; discard the leftover marinade. Cook without moving until well browned, about 5 minutes.
Finish the chicken: Flip and cook until the thickest part reads 165°F on an instant-read thermometer, 4-5 minutes more. Transfer to a board and rest for 5 minutes.

Toss the pasta: In a large bowl, combine the drained pasta, tomatoes, mozzarella pearls, chopped basil, chopped bacon, lemon juice, 1 tbsp olive oil, and 1/3 tsp kosher salt. Toss, adding splashes of the reserved pasta water until glossy.
Plate: Slice the chicken against the grain. Spoon the pasta onto plates, lay the chicken on top, and drizzle generously with the balsamic glaze. Finish with more basil and cracked black pepper.
tips: The original step pulled the chicken at 160°F to rest; it now cooks to 165°F in the pan, the USDA safe temperature for chicken.
